start.text: The answering horn: a long horn of black wood bound in brass, slung under a beam with its bell to the sea. It would take two to sound it, by the look of it, and a good pair of lungs.
A sailcloth bung is pushed into the bell, and tarred line crossed over it; more is wound round the mouthpiece, thick and tight, the way you'd bind a wound.
The lashing is just as tight. But somebody has wiped the salt off the brass, where a hand rests.
Out on the Teeth the Wrack burns gold, and the lashed bell is turned to it, waiting on Wenna.

open.text: The answering horn, unlashed: its bell open to the sea and the Wrack's light, the cut line coiled and hung off the seaward post. The brass is warm where hands have been.
It would take two to sound it. It has two, now.
